long_synopsis: Week 33 closed at 7:42 p.m., barely moved from the week before, a stillness that masked intense pressure across nearly every institution. The White House pushed to control election rules through executive order, investigated Democratic fundraising, and pressed partisan redistricting. Immigration enforcement expanded through spyware, no-bail detention, and family-reunification traps, while military language and infrastructure crept further into domestic life. Public health leadership was purged for resisting political pressure, and roughly 450,000 federal workers lost union protections. Courts pushed back repeatedly, blocking child deportations, reinstating a fired regulator, and restoring Harvard's funding, but enforcement often continued regardless. Congress split between transparency efforts on Epstein files and an attempt to reshape the memory of January 6. The moral floor accounting found breaches in nearly every recorded trait, a pattern its own analysis called collapsing, even as the clock itself scarcely stirred.
short_synopsis: The clock barely moved this week as executive assertion and institutional resistance ran nearly even. Elections, immigration, public health, and labor rights all came under pressure, while courts pushed back with real but incomplete effect, leaving a system straining at nearly every joint.
